key_insight: LLM-based coding agents can read environment source code and synthesize control policies that match or outperform conventional RL methods without task-specific RL training.
engineering_relevance: When readable environment models are available, direct policy synthesis could reduce interaction costs while producing inspectable decision rules.
method: Inspect environment source code to understand system dynamics.
Translate that knowledge into executable control policies.
Refine policies using online feedback or offline data.
evidence_signal: Across diverse decision-making benchmarks, synthesized policies matched or outperformed conventional RL with substantially less experience; source-code ablations and challenging-condition tests supported the value of readable world models.
watch_item: Practical deployment depends on access to accurate, readable world models; the abstract does not establish performance when source code is unavailable or mismatched to reality.
paper_title: Do We Still Need Reinforcement Learning When We Can Read the World Model?
